text: A decorator is a function that wraps another function to add behavior, without changing the original's code.
Shout takes a function, and defines an inner wrapper that calls it and shouts the result in uppercase.
It returns that wrapper, so the wrapper takes the place of the original function.
[chuckle] The at-sign syntax is the magic — at-shout above greet means greet gets wrapped automatically.
So calling greet now returns the upper-cased version, even though greet itself never mentions uppercase.
[sigh] Real decorators use star-args and double-star kwargs in the wrapper, so they work on any function.
This timing decorator records the start, runs the wrapped function, and prints how long it took.
Stack the at-timed above slow_add, and every call is measured for free.
[groan] Decorators are how Python adds logging, caching, and access checks cleanly — you'll see them everywhere in real frameworks.
Up next, closures. Tell me in the comments if this clicked.
